questions.stem: Can there be Data without Metadata, according to *I Am Datapedia!*?
options: Yes, as long as the data is unstructured
Yes, raw data never carries metadata
questions.explanation: The stated answer is No; Data without Metadata is not possible.

questions.stem: In the simplified Data vs Metadata illustration, what were Column Names labelled as?
questions.explanation: To simplify comprehension, Column Names were labelled as Metadata and the actual content as Data.

questions.stem: Column Names shown in a table illustrate which of the three traditional types of Metadata?
questions.explanation: Column Names are Technical Metadata, one of the three traditional types alongside Business and Operational.

options: Metadata that is ingrained within the content of the table
Metadata stored only in the data dictionary
Metadata created by the database vendor
The first metadata standard ever published
questions.explanation: Foundational Metadata is introduced as metadata that is ingrained within the content of the table itself.

questions.stem: Into which two types can Foundational Metadata be categorised?
questions.explanation: Foundational Metadata is categorised into Key Columns and Non-Key Columns.

questions.stem: What do Key Columns consist of?
options: Data representing the attributes of the Entity Type
Data representing the execution time of a job
Descriptions written by the data steward
Data that duplicates the Non-Key Columns
questions.explanation: Key Columns hold data that represents, relates to and defines the characteristics of the specific Entity Type.

questions.stem: What do Non-Key Columns consist of?
options: Data that defines the Entity Type
Data representing the attributes of the Key Columns within the same row
questions.explanation: Non-Key Columns provide additional details about the attributes found in the Key Columns of the corresponding row.

questions.stem: Which saying is credited to Daniel Lundin when asking whether data can exist without metadata?
options: Every table needs a primary key
One person's Metadata is another person's Data
questions.explanation: Daniel Lundin's statement that one person's Metadata is another person's Data underscores the need to grasp the fundamentals of Data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the three traditional types of Metadata?
options: All of these are traditional types
questions.explanation: Traditionally there are three types: Business, Technical and Operational; Foundational Metadata is newly introduced.

questions.stem: What role do Non-Key Columns play in relation to Key Columns?
options: They complement and extend the Key Columns, giving a more comprehensive view of the record
They are stored in a separate table
questions.explanation: Non-Key Columns complement and extend the information in the Key Columns, enriching the understanding of the specific record or entity.
